newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends lower as traders await OPEC, cold.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends lower as traders await OPEC, cold.

text.p: IPE Brent futures erased their gains near the closing bell on Friday and settled slightly weaker after heating oil fell sharply and traders took profits ahead of OPEC's meeting next week in Vienna.
Buyers also retreated on recent signs of progress in the limited Iraqi oil sale, but traders said activity was very choppy and thin after this week's volatility.

Diplomats said earlier this week that the U.N.-Iraq oil-for-food deal which would allow Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil over six months appeared to be making progress toward implementation in the first quarter of 1997.

"We have the OPEC meeting next week for one thing and...there is no real clear pattern on the charts for people to rely on," said Jeff Potter, managing director of Univest Ireland Ltd in Dublin, explaining the choppy price action.
Jan Brent last traded down eight cents at $23.05 a barrel, well off its session high of $23.54 scored earlier in the day.

Oil traders expected OPEC ministers to rollover their output ceiling of 25.03 million barrels per day for 1997 as the group enjoys an unexpected $30 billion bonus this year from sharply higher oil prices.
